title: Micro refine undo map
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal playbook for small, focused refactors where the goal is: minimal blast radius, straightforward undo, and post-merge followups that catch behavioral regressions early. This is a scratchpad — rough hypotheses, examples, and a checklist I can copy into PR descriptions.

Principles (short):
- Make every change reversible in <= 30min of work (rollback steps clear).
- Prefer additive changes that can be gated behind feature flags.
- Keep test surface explicit: unit + smoke + small canned integration where feasible.
- Document migration steps and state transitions in PR body.

Common small-refactor patterns I hit:
1) Rename + move helpers across packages (fn-level change). Risk: import breakages, implicit behaviors.
2) Split large function into two (local refactor). Risk: subtle ordering changes, timing.
3) Replace an optimization (manual batching tweak) with more generic code path. Risk: perf regressions under load.
4) Encapsulate KV-cache access behind interface. Risk: cache semantics changed (expiry, LRU).

Undo map template (copy into PR):
- What to revert: commit X..Y (or PR #) — list key files.
- Revert command: git revert -m 1 <merge-commit-sha> OR cherry-pick reverse commits (explicit commands).
- DB/State rollback: none / migrate-back is X (if migration applied).
- Feature-flag flip: toggle `ff.new-thing` to false in conf/service/flags → immediate fallback.
- Post-revert verification: run smoke pipeline (scripts/test/smoke.sh) + replicate failing trace if present.

Risk scoring (quick):
- Low = pure rename, no behavior change, covered by unit tests.
- Medium = refactor touches caching/ordering, has integration tests but limited load testing.
- High = changes runtime behavior, affects routing, or has no tests.

Checklist for PR description (minimal):
- Motivation: one-liner why this refactor matters.
- Risk: low/medium/high + short rationale.
- Undo plan: explicit commands and toggles.
- Tests added: list files + what they cover.
- Perf considerations: expected change (tokens/sec / p50 latency) or NA.
- Observability: logs/traces added (span names, tags).
- Migration: schema/memory/state changes and backout steps.

Test matrix suggestions (don't overdo):
- Unit tests: file-level, assert behavior for edge cases.
- Smoke: end-to-end happy path (script).
- Canary: land to canary branch / small fleet for 30 min under synthetic load.
- Local perf check: run `bench/simulate_load.sh --warmup 2m` and compare before/after; paste numbers in PR comment.

Examples / mini-cases I used recently (notes):
- Moving `kv_cache/manager.go` → `cache/kv/manager.go` and switching import alias broke an implicit nil-check path. Undo: revert PR commit; additionally add unit test that simulates nil entry lookup.
- Replacing `batcher.BatchNow()` call with `batcher.Enqueue()` to improve batching: under low concurrency this introduced a micro-latency (10–15ms). Rollback: flip feature flag `ff.batcher-v2` to false and revert PR. Added a smoke test that asserts median latency < 50ms under 5 concurrent clients.

Observability to add (quick list to paste in PR):
- metric: `refactor.<area>.error_rate` for first 24h
- trace span: `refactor.<area>.split` with tag `refactor.v=<sha>`
- debug log: when falling back to legacy path include `refactor_undo_hint=<revert_cmd>`

Post-merge followups (first 72h):
- Day 0 (merge): confirm CI smoke ok + canary deployment health. Add comment with canary link.
- Day 1: check error_rate and p95 latency dashboards for area. Leave note in PR.
- Day 2: run small deterministic test that exercises changed code path (script path `scripts/regressions/check_<area>.sh`).
- Day 3–7: monitor for logs flagged by new metric; if > threshold, prepare revert.

Decision heuristics (when to not refactor):
- No tests and no owner willing to add coverage in the PR → defer.
- Touches critical path (token generation loop) and expected perf impact > 5% → require canary + perf data pre-merge.

Handy git snippets (copyable):
- Revert a merge (if PR was merged as merge commit): git revert -m 1 <merge_commit_sha> && git push origin HEAD
- Create revert branch for hotfix: git checkout -b revert/PR-<num> && git revert -m 1 <merge_sha>
- Cherry-pick inverse (when commits are linear): git cherry-pick -n <commit_sha> && git commit -m "revert: ..."

Stuff to include in a small followup PR if I land refactor first:
- Add explicit unit tests for edge case(s) found during review.
- Add a short smoke script and include in PR CI for 24h post-merge (optional ephemeral job).
- Add a short doc block in the module README explaining invariants that must not change.

Open questions / TODOs (me):
- Template automation: create a small GH PR template snippet that injects the undo-map and checklist automatically for PRs touching `cache`, `batcher`, or `kv` folders. (ticket?)
- Standardize `refactor.*` metric naming across modules (talk to observability team).
- Small ergonomic script: `tools/refactor-undo-check.sh` that validates presence of revert instructions in PR body.

Random scratch bullets (raw):
- think about flag TTL defaults (1h vs 24h) for small experiments.
- ensure feature flags are visible in console with owner and revert cmd.
- prefer short-lived canaries (30–60m) for micro changes unless high-risk.

If I forget this in future, TL;DR: Make it reversible, add minimal tests, add an undo plan in PR, and watch metrics for 72 hours.

--Melissa

(Examples to pull into PR: revert commands above, smoke script path, and one-line risk justification)
